\section{Detailed Trace-Length Estimates}
\label{sec:length}

This section develops the boundary and conditional-skeleton trace bounds used
by the length mechanism.

For a closed triangle $T$ and a rectifiable target $E$, define
\[
 L_E(T)=\mathcal H^1(T\cap E).
\]
For the closures of a hypothetical open cover, the trace bound is
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal H^1(E)
 \le L_E(T_C)+\sum_{i=0}^5L_E(T_i).
 \label{eq:length-subadditivity}
\end{equation}
All estimates in this section concern full traces and therefore apply to
assigned measurable subsets of those traces.

The strategy uses only the perimeter $\partial H$ and the full skeleton
$S$, whose measures were recorded in \eqref{eq:target-lengths}.  Every
skeleton estimate below is conditional on its stated center and V triangle
hypotheses; no unconditional noncoverage assertion for $S$ is made.

\subsection{Conditional skeleton trace caps}

We now develop the skeleton estimate used only when the center is CE1 or CE2.
The first lemma is the center contribution.

\begin{lemma}[Center skeleton cap]
\label{lem:center-skeleton-cap}
If $T_C$ is a CE1 or CE2 C triangle and contains exactly one radial
midpoint, then
\[
 L_S(T_C)<\frac32.
\]
\end{lemma}

% Proof environment omitted (source: 03_strategy1_length.tex).

\begin{lemma}[Positive-support skeleton cap]
\label{lem:positive-support-skeleton-cap}
Let $T_i$ be the closure of an original open V triangle, so
$V_i\in\mathrm{int}(T_i)$.  If
\[
 \Haus(T_i\cap r_j)>0
 \quad\text{for some }j\in\{i-1,i+1\},
\]
then
\[
 L_S(T_i)<\frac32.
\]
\end{lemma}

% Proof environment omitted (source: 03_strategy1_length.tex).

\begin{lemma}[No-support skeleton cap]
\label{lem:no-support-skeleton-cap}
If a V triangle has $A_i+B_i\le1$ and
\[
 \Haus(T_i\cap r_{i-1})=\Haus(T_i\cap r_{i+1})=0,
\]
then
\[
 L_S(T_i)\le2.
\]
\end{lemma}

% Proof environment omitted (source: 03_strategy1_length.tex).

For the remaining cap, use the following selected supercritical cell.  In
local directions $u,v$ meeting at $120^\circ$, if a closed unit triangle
contains $0,au,bv,c(u+v)$ with $0\le a\le b\le1$ and $a+b>1$, then
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 &a^2+ab+b^2\le1,\qquad c\le\frac12,\\
 &(a^2-1)c^2+(2ab^2+b)c+(b^4-b^2)\le0,
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:supercritical-admissible-cell}
\end{equation}
where $c$ lies on the connected component containing $c=0$.

\begin{lemma}[Supercritical skeleton cap]
\label{lem:supercritical-skeleton-cap}
If $A_i+B_i>1$, then
\[
 L_S(T_i)<\frac32.
\]
\end{lemma}

% Proof environment omitted (source: 03_strategy1_length.tex).

\begin{lemma}[A positive-support adjacent exceptional triangle is forced]
\label{lem:positive-support-rescuer}
Suppose $T_C$ is CE1 or CE2 and, after symmetry,
$T_C\cap\{M_0,\ldots,M_5\}=\{M_0\}$.  If at least two V triangles are
supercritical, then for a supercritical index $s\ne0$ there is some
$j\in\{s-1,s+1\}$ such that
\[
 M_s\in U_j,
 \qquad
 \Haus(T_j\cap r_s)>0.
\]
\end{lemma}

\subsection{Vd1/Vd2 corner estimates}

We next isolate the much stronger trace loss caused by Vd1 and Vd2 geometry.
For the following two results use the temporary coordinates
\[
 X=V_0+x(V_5-V_0)+y(V_1-V_0).
\]
Thus $V_0=(0,0)$, $V_5=(1,0)$, $V_1=(0,1)$, $O=(1,1)$, and
$\lVert(x,y)\rVert^2=x^2+y^2-xy$.

\begin{proposition}[Vd1/Vd2 corner normal form]
\label{prop:vd-corner-normal-form}
Let $T$ be the closure of an original Vd1 or Vd2 triangle at $V_0$, and let
$a,b$ be its exact reaches toward $V_5,V_1$.  There is a unique $t>0$ such
that, with $d=\sqrt{t^2+t+1}$,
\[
 T=\left\{(x,y):
 \begin{aligned}
 x-(t+1)y&\le a,\\
 ty-(t+1)x&\le tb,\\
 tx+y&\le d-a-tb
 \end{aligned}\right\}.
 \label{eq:vd-normal-form}
\]
The raw traces, in coordinates measured from the indicated outer vertex, are
\[
 \begin{array}{c|c}
 r_0&0\le s\le\dfrac{d-a-tb}{t+1}\\[6pt]
 r_1&\dfrac{t(1-b)}{t+1}\le s\le\dfrac{d-a-tb-1}{t}\\[8pt]
 r_5&\dfrac{1-a}{t+1}\le s\le d-a-tb-t.
 \end{array}
 \label{eq:vd-ray-intervals}
\]
Intersecting with $[0,1]$ gives the actual traces.  Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 a+b<\frac12.
 \label{eq:vd-half-cap}
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}

% Proof environment omitted (source: 03_strategy1_length.tex).

\begin{lemma}[Vd2 adjacent-midpoint cap]
\label{lem:vd2-neighbor-midpoint-cap}
If an open role $U_i$ has Vd2 closure $T_i=\overline{U_i}$ and $T_i$
contains $M_{i-1}$ or $M_{i+1}$, then its
exact boundary reaches satisfy
\[
 a+b<\frac13.
\]
\end{lemma}

% Proof environment omitted (source: 03_strategy1_length.tex).

\subsection{Boundary trace caps}

The signed center normal form gives the CE1 and CE2 center contributions from
one formula; no separate maximal-interval calculation is needed here.

\begin{theorem}[Boundary trace table]
\label{thm:boundary-trace-table}
For closures of original open triangles, the following bounds hold:
\[
 \begin{array}{c|c|c}
 \text{triangle}&\text{hypothesis}&L_{\partial H}\\ \hline
 T_C&\mathrm{CE0}&0\\
 T_C&\mathrm{CE1}&\le\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}-\dfrac34\\[3pt]
 T_C&\mathrm{CE2}&<\dfrac12\\[3pt]
 T_i&\mathrm{Vd0},\ A_i+B_i\le1&\le1\\
 T_i&\mathrm{Vd0},\ A_i+B_i>1&\le\dfrac2{\sqrt3}\\[3pt]
 T_i&\mathrm{Vd1/Vd2}&<\dfrac12\\
 T_i&\text{T3-like}&<1.
 \end{array}
 \label{eq:boundary-trace-table}
\]
\end{theorem}

% Proof environment omitted (source: 03_strategy1_length.tex).

\subsection{Final length contradictions}

\begin{proposition}[Vd2 adjacent-midpoint branch]
\label{prop:ce2-vd2-midpoint-length}
Assume a CE2, $N_+=1$ configuration has exactly one Vd1/Vd2 triangle, that triangle
is $T_i$ of type Vd2 and contains $M_{i-1}$ or $M_{i+1}$, and all other V triangles are
Vd0.  Then the boundary cannot be covered.
\end{proposition}

% Proof environment omitted (source: 03_strategy1_length.tex).

\begin{proposition}[Branches closed by Method 1]
\label{prop:length-branches}
Direct length-sum obstructions close the following routing entries and hybrid
subcase:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item CE0, $N_+=0$;
 \item CE0, $N_+=1$, with a Vd1/Vd2 triangle;
 \item CE1/CE2 with $N_++N_{\mathrm{sp}}\ge3$;
 \item CE1/CE2, $N_+=0$, with a Vd1/Vd2 triangle;
 \item CE1, $N_+=1$, with exactly one Vd1/Vd2 triangle and no T3-like triangle;
 \item the CE2 hybrid subcase in which the Vd2 triangle $T_i$ contains
 $M_{i-1}$ or $M_{i+1}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}
